lines.text: Twenty times n is a perfect square. Fifty times n is a perfect cube!
lines.caption: Twenty times n is a perfect square. Fifty times n is a perfect cube!

lines.text: What is the smallest n that works?
lines.caption: What is the smallest n that works?

lines.text: Twenty is two times two times five. Fifty is two times five times five.
lines.caption: Twenty is two times two times five. Fifty is two times five times five.

lines.text: A square needs even counts. A cube needs multiples of three.
lines.caption: A square needs even counts. A cube needs multiples of three.

lines.text: The twos need two copies. The fives need one. So n is two times two times five.
lines.caption: The twos need two copies. The fives need one. So n is two times two times five.

lines.text: Twenty times twenty is four hundred, a square. Fifty times twenty is one thousand, a cube.
lines.caption: Twenty times twenty is four hundred, a square. Fifty times twenty is one thousand, a cube.

lines.text: Why does that work? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
lines.caption: Why does that work? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
